summary: Iteration 3 backend: 14/19 pytest cases pass. Stripe SDK switch verified — checkout returns real https://checkout.stripe.com cs_test_... session in mode=subscription with trial_period_days=7, billing_portal returns https://billing.stripe.com URL, /subscription/start-trial correctly returns 400, all baseline flows (signup/login/me/translation/daily-verse/verse-match 3-cap/history/favorites/TTS) regress green. CRITICAL BUG: every customer.subscription.* webhook event raises 'Webhook handler error: get' so the user document NEVER transitions trialing/active/canceled — 5 webhook-driven tests fail and is_premium stays false even after Stripe simulates trial start. Frontend paywall/settings code carries new iteration-3 strings (FIRST 7 DAYS ON US, $4.99, Start 7-day free trial, Manage subscription) but the disclosure paragraph still reads 'No auto-renewal — you choose when to renew' and '37 days for your first payment', which is misleading copy now that the architecture is real recurring auto-charge.

critical.issue: Handler logs 'Webhook handler error: get' for every subscription event, so _apply_subscription_to_user is never executed. User stays subscription_status='free' / is_premium=false after Stripe sends a trial-start, active, or cancel event. Reproduce: POST /api/webhook/stripe with body {type:'customer.subscription.created', data:{object:{id:'sub_x', status:'trialing', current_period_end:<unix>, metadata:{user_id:<uid>}, customer:'cus_x', cancel_at_period_end:false}}}. Response is 200 {received:true} (silently swallowed in try/except) but DB unchanged. Likely the stripe.Event.construct_from path produces a StripeObject for event['data']['object'] and either obj.get('metadata') or the chained .get inside _apply_subscription_to_user blows up — the catch-all logs only str(e)='get' so likely AttributeError on something accessed with .get. Fix: convert obj to a plain dict explicitly (dict(obj) doesn't deep-convert StripeObjects; need json.loads(json.dumps(obj))) BEFORE calling _apply_subscription_to_user, and ensure metadata access is .get('metadata',{}) not .get('metadata') or {}. Also confirm _apply_subscription_to_user receives a dict whose nested values are plain Python (current_period_end is int, status is str). This is blocking — without it Stripe webhooks cannot grant premium.

Lines 750-899 define a SECOND copy of POST /subscription/checkout, GET /subscription/status/{session_id}, and POST /webhook/stripe using the OLD emergentintegrations.payments.stripe (StripeCheckout, CheckoutSessionRequest, FIRST_PAYMENT_DAYS, SUBSCRIPTION_DAYS) — none of those names are imported/defined any more. They're dead code only because FastAPI matches the FIRST registered route at lines 573/626/693, but if anyone touches the route order or the dead bodies are accidentally executed, the server will throw NameError at runtime. Also _grant_premium_for_user at line 801 is dead. Strip the dead block (lines 750–899).

minor.issue: Top-level try/except logs only str(e) and returns 200 {received:true} even when handler completely failed to apply state. Re-raise as 500 (or at minimum return {received:true, processed:false, error:...}) so failures are visible to retries from Stripe.
return_url is hard-coded to '<origin>/(tabs)/settings'. The literal parens are URL-special chars — works in Expo Router web but worth url-encoding for safety.

rca_of_issue: RCA: POST /api/webhook/stripe handler at server.py line 693 catches a generic Exception, logs 'Webhook handler error: get'. The error originates either at line 727 `(obj.get('metadata') or {}).get('user_id')` or inside _apply_subscription_to_user `sub.get('status', 'free')`. event = stripe.Event.construct_from(json.loads(body), api_key) returns a stripe.Event whose `data.object` is a stripe.Subscription StripeObject. While StripeObject is dict-subclass, nested fields like `metadata` are themselves StripeObjects — calling .get on them works in current SDK versions, BUT chained access like sub_dict['status'] after assigning `sub_dict = obj if isinstance(obj, dict) else dict(obj)` may not deep-convert; dict(stripe_obj) only shallow-converts. Reproduction: see test_iteration3_subscription.py::TestWebhook::test_webhook_no_signature_dev_mode_accepts. Mitigation: replace `obj` extraction with `obj = json.loads(json.dumps(event['data']['object'], default=str))` to get a fully plain-dict tree; then all .get calls work. Alternative: use stripe SDK's `event.data.object.to_dict_recursive()`. Either fix unblocks all 5 failing tests.
